owner_directive: PROFITABLE PAIRS + DYNAMIC INVENTORY SELECTION; smallest viable implementation change that improves executable expected value

labels.MEASURED_L5: from the normalized L5 history; L5's own trades on Polymarket, not ours
labels.VENUE_CONFIRMED: our own PMUS orders, fills and settlements
labels.REPLAY: simulated openings and completions on harvested tape; NOT realized money
labels.BLOCKED: cannot be computed from available data; the missing input is named

action_mix_all_venues.reading: L5 opens rarely (4.0%) and then alternates same-side EXTEND (49.1%) with opposite-side COMPLETE (46.9%). He essentially never sells -- 2 of 71,984.

completion_pair_cost_by_time_to_expiry.reading: L5's mean completion cost is 0.963-0.973 at every horizon, and the share he pays ABOVE par rises from 15% to 27% as settlement approaches. He tolerates dearer completion near the end; he does not change his average.

completion_pair_cost_by_imbalance.reading: more imbalanced does NOT make him pay up. The above-par share FALLS as imbalance grows.

answers.accumulates_one_side_aggressively: YES -- EXTEND is 49.1% of all fills, the single largest action class
answers.buys_the_opposite_side: YES -- COMPLETE is 46.9%, and 17-27% of those cost more than the $1.00 the pair redeems
answers.stops_adding_exposure: NOT ISOLABLE from this dataset: it carries fills, not the quotes that rested unfilled, so a decision not to add leaves no row
answers.completes_pairs: YES -- 96.02% of BTC15m windows see at least one completion, median 52 per window
answers.changes_behaviour_near_settlement: YES -- the above-par share nearly doubles inside the last 30s (15.4% -> 26.7%) while the mean cost does not move

comparison_to_our_engine.finding: our ceiling is TIGHTER than L5's measured average completion cost. Tested in Phase D and it changed nothing: no completion in the replay ever priced between 0.96 and 0.97.

phase_B_policy_status: BLOCKED on one named input, and the block is the finding

phase_B_blocker.requirement: an independently calibrated probability estimate with explicit uncertainty, used to accumulate on the positive-EV side rather than the cheaper side
phase_B_blocker.settlement_rule: UP iff BRTI at window end >= BRTI at window start (CF Benchmarks Bitcoin Real-Time Index). The strike IS the window's own opening price, so the estimate needs the BRTI series, not the market's own price.
what_is_missing: no BRTI endpoint on gateway.polymarket.us: /v1/market/slug/<slug> returns assetPriceTerms with strike:null and priceToBeat:null, and 8 candidate chart/price routes all 404
cfbenchmarks.com, api.coinbase.com and api.binance.com are all refused by this environment's network policy
our own code has no BRTI fetcher -- only a prose statement of the settlement rule in l5_venue_adapter.py
the only local reference series, analysis/profit_search/tick/spot.json, is ~50 minutes on one day (epoch 1792940994..1792943972) and covers NONE of the 19 replay windows
phase_B_blocker.consequence: EV-based side selection, hedging assessed against both outcomes using an independent probability, and 'reduce exposure when the probability estimate changes' are all unimplementable today. They are not refused on evidence; they have no input. The market price is the only probability available, and using it makes the EV test circular.
phase_B_blocker.what_would_unblock_it: a BRTI (or equivalent BTC reference) series at 1s-5s resolution, live for execution and historical for replay. One allowed outbound host, or a recorder on existing infrastructure, is the whole requirement.

C1_completion_deadline.defect: `L5_TS_CANCEL_MARGIN_S=300` overrode the code floor of 180, pulling cancel_cutoff to T+600 -- exactly ENTRY_CUTOFF_S -- so COMPLETE_CUTOFF_S=720 was unreachable and the engine stopped reducing risk at the same instant it stopped taking it. A code feature cancelled by configuration.
C1_completion_deadline.live_signature: PAST_TERMINAL on 143 book-completion decisions from T+601 to T+714; PAST_COMPLETE_CUTOFF only from T+725
C1_completion_deadline.correction: stop widening: the floor of 180 governs, terminal T+720, completion outlives opening by 120s

safety.note: the pre-TTL rationale for widening to 300 (a 600s rest tripping the watchdog) no longer applies; the TTL bounds age structurally

C1_completion_deadline.side_effect: TOO_LATE_TO_WITHDRAW becomes unreachable on a full-length window because PAST_ENTRY_CUTOFF (600) is checked first. It is NOT dead code: t_end is the VENUE's close and an early close makes it binding again, which is pinned by test.

C2_fee_schedule.question: verify the reported 2026-10-19 schedule change against official venue records
C2_fee_schedule.method: gateway.polymarket.us/v1/market/slug/<slug> carries feeCoefficient and resolved markets keep it; queried individually across 13 dates
C2_fee_schedule.verdict: the 2026-10-19 change is NOT corroborated. No step exists at that date.
C2_fee_schedule.limit_of_evidence: markets before ~2026-09-30 return 404 (retention floor), so a change at or before that date cannot be ruled out. The docs.polymarket.us read of 0.06 on 2026-09-13 sits below the floor and cannot be re-verified.
C2_fee_schedule.consequence: all our live trade dates (2026-10-11..2026-11-02) sit inside one verified coefficient, so NO per-date split is warranted; a date-split would invent a change the venue does not show
C2_fee_schedule.defect_found_and_fixed: l5_cross_shadow.py and pmus_cross_shadow_live.py both carried TAKER_THETA 0.06, understating the taker charge by 14% and flattering every crossing cost computed with them. Both corrected to 0.0695. Neither is on the money path or in the image COPY list; l5_two_sided_probe, l5_queue_measurement and l5_strand_policy_replay were already correct.
C2_fee_schedule.taker_tier: base rate; reduced tiers begin at $250,000 prior-calendar-month volume and we are orders of magnitude below

C3_duplicate_suppression.defect: action_key was (market, side, price) alone, which cannot distinguish a re-fire at an unchanged book (must suppress) from the first leg of a SECOND pair at the same price after the first completed (must allow). That is why L5_TS_CONTINUOUS_INVENTORY regressed pair-after-pair.
C3_duplicate_suppression.fix: an optional `epoch` from inventory_epoch(up_q, dn_q) -- a fingerprint of REALIZED inventory that moves only when a fill lands. Still content-addressed: no clock, no counter, no round. epoch=None is byte-for-byte the old key.
C3_duplicate_suppression.residual_opening: flag B stays bounded: decide() takes imbalance_cap explicitly and defaults it to D(0), so no ADD is permitted unless a caller states a bound it can know before the order. Pinned by test.
C3_duplicate_suppression.flags: BOTH REMAIN OFF. This closes a precondition for promotion; it promotes nothing.

phase_D_replay.basis: REPLAY -- 19 harvested BTC15m windows with two-sided tape, 2026-10-28..2026-11-02, chronological 60/40 split (11 train / 8 holdout). Openings AND completions are simulated. Conservative fill rule: a resting maker order fills only when the wire trades through its price; queue position is ignored, which is OPTIMISTIC on fills. Fees at the verified 0.0695 taker / 0.0125 maker rebate, banker's cent. No look-ahead and no guaranteed fills. Incentives counted at ZERO.

calibration_against_realized.note: the replay matches realized residual economics closely and OVERSTATES matched margin by ~55%, so it is biased toward promoting a change

single_factor_decomposition.verdict: BEST HOLDOUT; train unchanged, so the gain is not fitted
NO EFFECT -- identical to baseline; no completion in the sample priced between 0.96 and 0.97
identical to A1 -- the cap contributes nothing
worse holdout than A1 alone; the floor removal drags it
WORSE in both halves; opening depth is not the lever

regime_split_holdout.reading: every gain is concentrated in high-volatility windows, which is where the book moves enough for a later completion to become reachable at all

phase_D_replay.hedge_cost: 0.0000 in every arm -- no completion above $1.00 ever fired, so no loss-making hedge was taken anywhere in the replay
phase_D_replay.fidelity_to_L5: still far off: the replay completes 0.3-0.4 pairs per window against L5's median of 52 on BTC15m, and our matched:residual ratio cannot approach his 5.34 at a 3-contract clip and $12 of cash

candidate.change: the completion-deadline correction ALONE (C1), plus the two accounting corrections (C2, C3) which do not touch the money path
explicitly_NOT_changed: completion ceiling stays 0.96 -- measured no effect, and L5's 0.97 average did not transfer
taker margin floor stays $0.25 -- removing it is a train-only gain and worsens the holdout
opening depth stays 2 -- depth 1 is worse in both halves
no risk limit, exposure cap, clip size or band moved
candidate.honest_caveat: the corrected arm is STILL LOSS-MAKING in replay and no-trade still beats it on this sample. The fix reduces the loss; it does not make the strategy profitable. And on the four VENUE-CONFIRMED fills of 2026-11-02 it recovers exactly nothing, because those fills landed at T+21..T+130 and the deadline never bound. Its value is for LATE fills, a state the live campaign has not yet produced.

remaining_risks: the replay simulates openings; only 4 of the 19 windows ever had a real order, so the 19-window result is not realized money
no queue model: our own pre-submit records carry our_position_within_level UNKNOWN against touch depth of 52,000-100,000 shares for a 2-contract clip
n=8 holdout windows. A +$0.57 difference on 8 windows is not statistically established

the 89-window venue ledger spans a period in which the executor was repeatedly modified, so pooling it as one strategy's history is invalid and its chronological split aligns with a regime break at 2026-10-26/27
TOO_LATE_TO_WITHDRAW is now unreachable on full-length windows; the early-close path is pinned by test but has never been exercised live
